findings.description: `targetHolds` calls `git ls-tree` without `--full-tree`, so a session that plants `core.worktree` in the shared `.git/config` narrows the listing to nothing; `targetHolds` returns `[]` and the gate falls back to the pre-157 fail-open, judging an existing file the before-measure omits against the cap of 50 instead of the +15 rise.

The target-tree fallback only matches when a custom adapter's `FileComplexity.file` uses git's repo-relative spelling. If a `.pupitre/adapter.yml` complexity command prints absolute paths, neither `before.get` nor `held.has` matches, so every touched existing file is still judged against the cap of 50. That leaves open the 'spell a path differently' half of 145's partial-command route, which ADR 0157 lists as closed.

The call-site comment above `measuresComplexity` repeats the `targetHolds` JSDoc in its clause "only a file the target lacks, by its own path or its source's, is new (decision 157)", which AGENTS.md §Comments says to delete. Keep the decision-145 half and drop or shorten the 157 clause.

process_issues.description: `bash scripts/adr-index.sh` needed approval under the CI command lock, so the reviewer couldn't confirm that the generated ADR index passes `--check` or that 0157 is the next free number. The security reviewer hit the same block and found the ADRs by grepping `docs/adr/` instead.
